claims.text: Wear performance of high-entropy-alloy protective coatings is primarily governed by the interplay between grain-boundary-mediated plasticity and formation of a continuous self-lubricating oxide film at grain boundaries.
A high grain-boundary density in nanocrystalline coatings promotes rapid and uniform oxide formation during wear.
The resulting oxide film reduces friction.
The resulting oxide film reduces wear rate.
Increasing grain size reduces grain-boundary density.
Reducing grain-boundary density diminishes the continuity and effectiveness of the lubricious oxide layer.
Thermal annealing can increase the coating's average grain size from approximately 20 nm to 40–100 nm or more.
Air or oxidizing-atmosphere annealing at approximately 300–400 °C for varied durations can produce systematic grain growth.
Fine nanocrystalline grains facilitate formation of a thin, continuous, self-lubricating oxide layer during wear.
A thin, continuous, self-lubricating oxide layer minimizes adhesive wear.
A thin, continuous, self-lubricating oxide layer minimizes micro-plowing.
Annealing-induced grain growth changes plastic-deformation behavior and thereby changes wear rate.
The balance between grain-boundary strengthening and oxide lubrication governs overall wear performance.
Increasing average grain size from approximately 20 nm to approximately 40 nm enhances oxide-film continuity and effectiveness.
Increasing average grain size from approximately 20 nm to approximately 40 nm reduces wear rate relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Grain growth beyond approximately 100 nm reduces grain-boundary strengthening.
Grain growth beyond approximately 100 nm diminishes oxide-film continuity.
Grain growth beyond approximately 100 nm increases wear rate under otherwise identical sliding conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies from room temperature to approximately 200 °C in ambient or mildly oxidizing atmospheres.
The proposed mechanism may not apply in vacuum or inert atmospheres, or at temperatures where oxidation kinetics are substantially altered.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism state that increasing grain size and reducing grain-boundary density diminish oxide-film continuity, whereas the predicted outcome states that moderate grain growth from about 20 nm to 40 nm enhances oxide-film continuity and effectiveness. No intermediate optimum or additional mechanism is supplied to reconcile these opposite directional claims.
